$comment: Receipts for the numbers this repository publishes in prose and on the site: the meta bar in docs/index.html (papers / days), README (filter-mode count, per-day spread, weekly archive W34-W37, config keywords and caps, delivery switches, the two-collector claim), docs/llms.txt and docs/llms-full.txt (feed size, weekly pages, per-day cap, sources) and docs/sitemap.xml. Every figure is recomputed from the committed docs/ tree and config.yaml by a stdlib-only python3 one-liner — no network and no installed package, so each expect holds on a bare runner; the site-rebuild receipt runs the repo's own scripts/generate_site.py and asserts the committed pages are byte-identical to a rebuild rather than a stale copy. .github/workflows/claims.yml runs the lot weekly and on every push.

claims.claim: The site meta bar counts 574 papers in all (`id="stat-papers"` in docs/index.html, rendered as "574 篇论文").
claims.value: counter == papers in the committed reports
claims.metric: the home page's paper counter versus the papers found in the committed digests
claims.method: scripts/generate_site.py sums parse_papers() over every dated report — docs/*.md is the system of record and "## n." is the record separator (scripts/reports.py splits on it) — and substitutes the total into the template's stat span. The check redoes that sum from the committed markdown and asserts it equals the published number, so a hand-edited stat line, or a report the generator parses differently, cannot pass.
claims.repro: python3 -c "import re,glob,pathlib;print(sum(len(re.findall(r'^## \d+\.\s+', pathlib.Path(f).read_text(encoding='utf-8'), re.M)) for f in glob.glob('docs/????-??-??.md')))"

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re, glob, pathlib
daily = sorted(glob.glob('docs/????-??-??.md'))
papers = sum(len(re.findall(r'^## \d+\.\s+', pathlib.Path(f).read_text(encoding='utf-8'), re.M)) for f in daily)
published = re.search(r'id=\"stat-papers\">(\d+)', pathlib.Path('docs/index.html').read_text(encoding='utf-8')).group(1)
assert str(papers) == published, (papers, published)
print('the site counter equals the number of papers in the committed reports')"

expect.equals: the site counter equals the number of papers in the committed reports

claims.claim: The site meta bar counts 61 days (`id="stat-dates"` in docs/index.html, rendered as "61 天") — one per committed daily digest.
claims.metric: the home page's day counter versus the dated files on disk
claims.method: The generator counts the dated reports it parsed with at least one paper (docs/*.md as database) and writes that into the same stat span the paper total goes into. The check counts the same files with the same glob.

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re, pathlib
d = pathlib.Path('docs')
n = len(list(d.glob('????-??-??.md')))
published = re.search(r'id=\"stat-dates\">(\d+)', (d / 'index.html').read_text(encoding='utf-8')).group(1)
assert str(n) == published, (n, published)
print('the site counter equals the number of committed digests')"

expect.equals: the site counter equals the number of committed digests

claims.claim: docs/index.md links every committed daily digest and nothing else: 61 dated entries, a one-to-one match with docs/YYYY-MM-DD.md on disk.
claims.metric: dated files on disk versus the dated links in docs/index.md
claims.method: scripts/common.py:prepend_index_entry keeps the "## 历史记录" list in front of the newest digest, so the index is written by the daily run and the files are written by the same run. The check asserts both directions (nothing linked that is missing, nothing on disk that is unlinked) and that no date is listed twice, which a deleted or hand-renamed report would break.

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re, pathlib
d = pathlib.Path('docs')
disk = sorted(p.name for p in d.glob('????-??-??.md'))
linked = re.findall(r'\]\((\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\.md)', (d / 'index.md').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
assert sorted(linked) == disk and len(set(linked)) == len(linked), (len(linked), len(set(linked)), len(disk))
print('every digest listed in docs/index.md, no orphan on either side')"

expect.equals: every digest listed in docs/index.md, no orphan on either side

claims.claim: Every committed weekly report has a rendered page, and each is in the sitemap.
claims.value: one page per weekly-*.md, all in the sitemap
claims.metric: weekly-*.md on disk vs weekly-*.html rendered vs weekly locs in the sitemap
claims.method: the check compares the three sets; a new weekly report that is never rendered, or a rendered page missing from the sitemap, fails. It deliberately does not pin a count: one weekly page is added every week.
claims.repro: ls docs/weekly-*.md | wc -l; ls docs/weekly-*.html | wc -l

claims.claim: Every digest that records its filtering mode records the no-key fallback, and the README states that without quoting a count — a count here grows every day and would go stale on its own.
claims.value: all recorded mode lines are the no-key fallback
claims.metric: digests carrying the mode line versus those carrying the no-key wording
claims.method: the mode line first appears only for digests written after 2026-08-21; the check requires every one of them to be the no-key fallback, and requires the README to make that statement without a number, because a number there would change with the archive
claims.repro: grep -c '本期筛选方式' docs/2026-*.md | grep -v ':0' | wc -l

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re, pathlib
files = sorted(pathlib.Path('docs').glob('????-??-??.md'))
mode = [f for f in files if '本期筛选方式' in f.read_text(encoding='utf-8')]
nokey = [f for f in mode if '本期筛选方式：热度回退（未配置 LLM）' in f.read_text(encoding='utf-8')]
assert mode == nokey, [f.name for f in mode if f not in nokey]
assert mode == [f for f in files if f.stem >= '2026-08-21'], (len(mode), mode[:1], mode[-1:])
readme = pathlib.Path('README.md').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
# README 不得给出一个会随日报增长的数字：那句话今天就是被这条断言抓住的
assert 'Every digest that records its filtering mode records the no-key fallback' in readme, 'README sentence missing'
assert not re.search(r'The \\d+ committed reports that record their mode', readme), 'README states a count that grows'
print('every recorded mode line is the no-key fallback; README states it without a count')"

expect.equals: every recorded mode line is the no-key fallback; README states it without a count

claims.claim: config.yaml ships 7 keywords and 4 arXiv categories (cs.AI, cs.CL, cs.IR, cs.MA), and README plus docs/llms-full.txt quote every one of them by name.
claims.metric: entries under keywords: and categories: in config.yaml, cross-checked against the prose that documents them
claims.method: The two lists are the query matrix the arXiv collector builds (scripts/sources/arxiv_source.py), so they are the package's topic definition rather than documentation; the README configuration block and the llms-full answer repeat them for readers. The check counts the committed config and fails if either document stops naming a keyword or category — the doc-rot case where config.yaml is edited and the prose is not.

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re, pathlib
t = pathlib.Path('config.yaml').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
kw = re.findall(r'^  - \"([^\"]+)\"$', t, re.M)
cats = re.findall(r'^  - \"(cs\.[A-Z]+)\"', t, re.M)
assert len(kw) == 7 and len(cats) == 4, (kw, cats)
for doc in ('README.md', 'docs/llms-full.txt'):
    text = pathlib.Path(doc).read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    missing = [k for k in kw + cats if k not in text]
    assert not missing, (doc, missing)
print(len(kw), 'keywords,', len(cats), 'categories:', ' '.join(cats))"

expect.equals: 7 keywords, 4 categories: cs.AI cs.CL cs.IR cs.MA

claims.claim: The per-day cap is 10 papers and the weekly roundup is a Top 15 (`max_papers: 10`, `weekly_max_papers: 15`); the committed archive honours both — no daily exceeds 10, every weekly holds exactly 15.
claims.metric: the two config values, the largest "## n." count per daily report, and the heading count of each weekly report
claims.method: config.yaml is the only place the caps live (scripts/main.py reads max_papers, scripts/weekly.py weekly_max_papers); README and docs/llms-full.txt both publish the same pair. The check pins the config and the archive together, so raising the cap without the prose, or writing a digest that ignores it, fails.

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re, pathlib
t = pathlib.Path('config.yaml').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
cap = re.search(r'^max_papers: (\d+)', t, re.M).group(1)
wcap = re.search(r'^weekly_max_papers: (\d+)', t, re.M).group(1)
assert (cap, wcap) == ('10', '15'), (cap, wcap)
per_day = [len(re.findall(r'^## \d+\.\s+', p.read_text(encoding='utf-8'), re.M)) for p in pathlib.Path('docs').glob('????-??-??.md')]
weekly = sorted({len(re.findall(r'^## \d+\.\s+', p.read_text(encoding='utf-8'), re.M)) for p in pathlib.Path('docs').glob('weekly-????-W??.md')})
assert max(per_day) == int(cap) and weekly == [int(wcap)], (max(per_day), weekly)
print('max_papers', cap, 'observed max', max(per_day), '| weekly_max_papers', wcap, 'observed', weekly[0])"

claims.claim: Delivery ships with the Feishu channel on and email off (`notify: feishu: true / email: false`), and both senders exist in scripts/notifier.py.
claims.metric: the notify: switches in config.yaml and the presence of send_feishu/send_email in the notifier
claims.method: The README Multi-channel row (Feishu messages / Email subscriptions / GitHub Pages) and its Configuration block publish these defaults. Email needs SMTP_* secrets and an opt-in, so the switch is meaningful: a fork that adds the secrets but not `email: true` gets no mail. The check reads the committed config and the two function definitions the daily run calls.

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re, pathlib
t = pathlib.Path('config.yaml').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
notify = re.search(r'^notify:\n((?:  \S+: \S+\n)+)', t, re.M).group(1)
feishu = re.search(r'feishu: (\S+)', notify).group(1)
email = re.search(r'email: (\S+)', notify).group(1)
assert (feishu, email) == ('true', 'false'), (feishu, email)
src = pathlib.Path('scripts/notifier.py').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
assert 'def send_feishu(' in src and 'def send_email(' in src
print('notify.feishu', feishu, '| notify.email', email, '| send_feishu + send_email implemented')"

expect.equals: notify.feishu true | notify.email false | send_feishu + send_email implemented

claims.claim: Exactly two collectors are implemented — arXiv and HuggingFace — matching the two `sources:` switches, and Papers With Code is not one of them: the name survives only as a `paperswithcode` key in the notifier's source-to-emoji lookup (README FAQ and docs/llms-full.txt both say so).
claims.metric: files in scripts/sources/, the sources: switches in config.yaml, and the files under scripts/ that still mention paperswithcode
claims.method: scripts/main.py imports the two collectors directly. The check pins the collector directory to the two names the prose promises, the config to the same pair, and the Papers With Code mention to scripts/notifier.py — the claim that it was never implemented is only true while no collector file carries the name.

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re, pathlib
src = sorted(p.name for p in pathlib.Path('scripts/sources').glob('*.py') if not p.name.startswith('__'))
t = pathlib.Path('config.yaml').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
assert src == ['arxiv_source.py', 'huggingface_source.py'], src
sw = re.search(r'^sources:\n((?:  \S+: \S+\n)+)', t, re.M).group(1)
assert re.findall(r'(\S+): (\S+)', sw) == [('arxiv', 'true'), ('huggingface', 'true')], sw
hits = sorted(p.name for p in pathlib.Path('scripts').rglob('*.py') if 'paperswithcode' in p.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
assert hits == ['notifier.py'], hits
print('two collectors', ' '.join(src), '| switches arxiv+huggingface only | paperswithcode only as the emoji key in', hits[0])"

expect.equals: two collectors arxiv_source.py huggingface_source.py | switches arxiv+huggingface only | paperswithcode only as the emoji key in notifier.py

claims.claim: The committed archive runs 4 to 10 papers per day, the 10 being the configured cap and the 4 its thinnest day (README: "At most max_papers (10) survive per day (the committed archive runs 4–10)").
claims.metric: per-digest paper counts, as a range rather than a total
claims.method: A day with no surviving paper is skipped entirely rather than committed empty (the workflow refuses to commit a run with no new report), which is why the archive has 61 days out of a longer calendar span. The check states the real floor and ceiling of the committed data, so it fails if a digest is written with more than the cap or the spread claim drifts.
claims.repro: python3 -c "import re,pathlib;c=[len(re.findall(r'^## \d+\.\s+', p.read_text(encoding='utf-8'), re.M)) for p in pathlib.Path('docs').glob('????-??-??.md')];print(min(c), max(c))"

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re, pathlib
counts = [len(re.findall(r'^## \d+\.\s+', p.read_text(encoding='utf-8'), re.M)) for p in sorted(pathlib.Path('docs').glob('????-??-??.md'))]
assert (min(counts), max(counts)) == (4, 10), (min(counts), max(counts))
print('every digest holds between 4 and 10 papers')"

expect.equals: every digest holds between 4 and 10 papers

claims.metric: feed item order and the 50-paper cap, independent of how many weeks have passed
claims.method: the feed leads with one item per weekly roundup page and then carries the 50 newest papers; the check asserts that structure rather than a count of weeks, which changes every Monday (it said '4 weekly pages' until a fifth week arrived)

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re, pathlib
f = pathlib.Path('docs/feed.xml').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
titles = re.findall(r'<title>(.*?)</title>', f, re.S)[1:]
weekly = [t for t in titles if 'Weekly roundup' in t]

expect.equals: weekly roundups first, then papers, capped at 50

claims.claim: The sitemap lists exactly the real HTML pages and nothing else: the home page, every weekly page and every daily page, with no `.md` target and no missing page.
claims.value: home + every weekly-*.html + every YYYY-MM-DD.html, set-equal both ways
claims.metric: loc entries in docs/sitemap.xml vs the HTML pages committed under docs/
claims.method: docs/.nojekyll disables Jekyll, so `docs/YYYY-MM-DD.md` is served as text/markdown and the page for that day is the generated `YYYY-MM-DD.html`; scripts/generate_site.py builds the sitemap from the home page, the weekly reports and every daily report. The check asserts set equality both ways — a page on disk missing from the sitemap, or a sitemap URL with no page (including any `.md`), fails.

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re, pathlib
d = pathlib.Path('docs')
locs = {u.rsplit('/', 1)[-1] or 'index.html' for u in re.findall(r'<loc>([^<]+)</loc>', d.joinpath('sitemap.xml').read_text())}
disk = {p.name for p in d.glob('*.html') if p.name != 'template.html'}
print('sitemap', len(locs), 'disk', len(disk))
assert locs == disk, ('in sitemap only', sorted(locs - disk), 'on disk only', sorted(disk - locs))
assert not any(l.endswith('.md') for l in locs)"

claims.claim: The home page inlines the 30 newest daily reports (the same 30 dates in its selector) while the meta bar counts all 61 committed dailies — the cap README describes as "the daily content is inlined into the home page".
claims.metric: inlined sections and selector options versus the newest 30 digests
claims.method: scripts/generate_site.py renders sections and selector options from a slice of the newest 30 reports but sums the paper and day counters over all of them, so the two numbers on the page legitimately differ. The check pins the slice to the newest 30 in order and asserts the selector and the sections agree, which a change of window would break.

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re, pathlib
h = pathlib.Path('docs/index.html').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
secs = re.findall(r'class=\"date-section\" data-date=\"(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\"', h)
opts = re.findall(r'<option value=\"(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\"', h)
dates = sorted((p.stem for p in pathlib.Path('docs').glob('????-??-??.md')), reverse=True)
assert secs == opts == dates[:30], (len(secs), len(opts), secs[:3], opts[:3])
print('the newest 30 digests are inlined, and the selector lists the same 30')"

expect.equals: the newest 30 digests are inlined, and the selector lists the same 30

claims.claim: Rebuilding the site from the committed docs/ tree reproduces the committed pages byte for byte: `python3 scripts/generate_site.py` leaves `git status --porcelain docs/` empty.
claims.metric: git status of docs/ after running the repo's own generator on a clean checkout
claims.method: The generator is the only writer of docs/index.html, feed.xml, sitemap.xml, robots.txt and the weekly pages, so a dirty tree after a rebuild means the committed site no longer matches its source. feed.xml's lastBuildDate and the sitemap's home lastmod are derived from the newest committed report date rather than the wall clock for exactly this reason — a clock stamp would dirty the tree on every run, including on CI.

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import subprocess, sys
subprocess.run([sys.executable, 'scripts/generate_site.py'], check=True, capture_output=True)
out = subprocess.run(['git', 'status', '--porcelain', 'docs/'], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
assert out == '', out
print('regenerated docs/ with scripts/generate_site.py: git status --porcelain docs/ is empty')"

expect.equals: regenerated docs/ with scripts/generate_site.py: git status --porcelain docs/ is empty

claims.claim: Every committed daily digest has its own HTML page, every one of those pages carries a description, a canonical URL, an Open Graph block and Article JSON-LD, and their titles are distinct — the archive is not only inlined into the home page.
claims.value: one page per digest, all with head metadata, all in the sitemap
claims.metric: docs/YYYY-MM-DD.md on disk vs YYYY-MM-DD.html rendered vs dated locs in the sitemap, plus the presence of the four head elements on each page
claims.method: scripts/generate_site.py renders one page per committed digest (render_daily_page) and lists it in the sitemap. The check compares the three sets and inspects every page's head; a day rendered without metadata, or a digest with no page, fails.
claims.repro: ls docs/????-??-??.md | wc -l; ls docs/????-??-??.html | wc -l; grep -c '<loc>' docs/sitemap.xml

claims.claim: Every page or SVG in this repository that animates also handles `prefers-reduced-motion` — motion here is decoration, and the artefact must stay complete when it is off.
claims.value: no animated file without a reduced-motion branch
claims.metric: files containing an animation primitive vs files containing `prefers-reduced-motion`
claims.method: the check walks every committed page and SVG and covers all four ways one can move — CSS animations/keyframes, SVG SMIL, requestAnimationFrame, and the CSS animations inside an SVG hero — requiring a `prefers-reduced-motion` reference wherever it finds one. SVG heroes are included because GitHub renders them through : scripts do not run, CSS animations do, and a hero that loops forever is exactly what a reduced-motion branch is for.

check.cmd:
python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib, re

MOVES = re.compile(r'animation\s*:|@keyframes|<animate\b|<animateTransform\b|requestAnimationFrame')
RELAX = 'prefers-reduced-motion'
pages = sorted(set(
    list(pathlib.Path('.').glob('*.html'))
    + list(pathlib.Path('.').glob('docs/*.html'))
    + list(pathlib.Path('.').glob('assets/*.svg'))
    + list(pathlib.Path('.').glob('assets/readme/*.svg'))
))
pages = [p for p in pages if p.name != 'template.html']
animated, missing = 0, []
for p in pages:
    t = p.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
    if MOVES.search(t):
        animated += 1
        if RELAX not in t:
            missing.append(str(p))
print('files', len(pages), 'animated', animated, 'missing', missing)
assert animated and not missing
PY

claims.claim: Every daily page is numbered as an issue: its "Issue N" is the digest's position counted from the oldest report, so the newest digest is #N (N = committed digests). The home page's issue head carries the same number — it is derived, never hand-typed.
claims.value: issue numbers are exactly 1..N, newest == N
claims.metric: the 期号 on each docs/YYYY-MM-DD.html and #issue-no on the home page versus the ordered digest list
claims.method: scripts/generate_site.py numbers the ordered reports list (oldest = 1) and writes it into each daily page's kicker and into the home page's issue head (#issue-no, alongside each section's data-issue). The check rebuilds the same ordering from docs/*.md and asserts the numbering is contiguous 1..N, that the oldest is #1, and that the newest is #N — a hand-editedor off-by-one number fails.

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re, pathlib
d = pathlib.Path('docs')
dates = sorted(p.stem for p in d.glob('????-??-??.md'))
n = len(dates)
head = re.search(r'id=\"issue-no\">(\d+)', (d / 'index.html').read_text(encoding='utf-8')).group(1)
assert int(head) == n, ('home issue head', head, n)
seen = []
for date in dates:
    h = (d / (date + '.html')).read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    m = re.search(r'issue-kicker\">[^<]*?Issue (\d+)', h)
    assert m, date
    seen.append(int(m.group(1)))
assert sorted(seen) == list(range(1, n + 1)), sorted(seen)[:5]
assert seen[0] == 1 and seen[-1] == n, (dates[0], seen[0], dates[-1], seen[-1])
print('issue numbers 1..%d contiguous, oldest #1, newest #%d' % (n, n))"

claims.claim: The published interface is English: no CJK ideograph and no full-width punctuation survives in the rendered text of any generated page (home, 62 daily pages, 5 weekly pages). Article titles and abstracts are the original English source text, and the Chinese tags the pipeline writes into the Markdown (`高票/有代码`, `最新论文`) are mapped to English labels for display, while `data-tags` and URL hashes keep stable English slugs.
claims.metric: CJK ideographs and full-width punctuation left after stripping <script>, <style> and HTML comments from every generated page
claims.method: scripts/generate_site.py renders the interface from English literals and maps data-layer tags through _tag_label()/_tag_slug(). The check strips inline script/style blocks and comments (developer comments stay Chinese by house style) and asserts nothing from U+3000-303F, U+FF00-FFEF or the CJK ideograph ranges remains in what a reader actually sees.

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re, pathlib
cjk = re.compile(r'[\u3000-\u303f\uff00-\uffef\u4e00-\u9fff]')
strip = lambda s: re.sub(r'<script.*?</script>|<style.*?</style>|<!--.*?-->', '', s, flags=re.S)
pages = [p for p in sorted(pathlib.Path('docs').glob('*.html')) if p.name != 'template.html']
bad = {p.name: cjk.findall(strip(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8')))[:3] for p in pages if cjk.search(strip(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8')))}
assert not bad, bad
print('all %d generated pages render English text only' % len(pages))"

expect.regex: all \d+ generated pages render English text only
